ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a synchronous generator symbol, which after being connected to the bus passes through a box-shaped circuit breaker/switch and a section of line, and delivers to the infinite bus with diagonal-line marking on the right side; the generator side is labeled 1.0∠δ pu, the infinite bus side is labeled 1.0∠0 pu, and on the line there is a rightward power arrow labeled 1.0 pu. Reasoning: The original system is a lossless single-machine infinite-bus system, the original operating point delivers 1.0 pu to the infinite bus, and the critical clearing time is 0.28 s. The electric power of a lossless system can be expressed by the power-angle relation Pe = Pmax sin δ. If another identical synchronous generator is connected in parallel, and each generator is made to supply only 0.5 pu, then compared with the original single generator bearing 1.0 pu, the load power of each unit is smaller, and the corresponding initial power angle δ is smaller. A smaller initial power angle means that the equal-area margin of transient stability increases, therefore the allowable clearing time after the fault becomes longer.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as a generator feeding an infinite bus through a breaker and a lossless reactance, with 1.0 pu voltage magnitudes and power-angle δ. Use the text to note the original operating point transfers 1.0 pu and has CCT = 0.28 s. For the modified system, two identical parallel generators each supply 0.5 pu. Model each/equivalent machine with the lossless power-angle relation P_e = P_max sin δ. Because each generator is less heavily loaded, the initial δ is smaller and the equal-area stability margin is larger than in the single-generator 1.0 pu case. Therefore the critical clearing time must increase beyond 0.28 s.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: The swing equation gives rotor acceleration as d²δ/dt² = (P_m - P_e)/M.
